entities.name: Grigol Hamam
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Grigor (Grigol) Hamam was a late ninth-century ruler of Hereti (in Arran/Caucasian Albania) who, according to Georgian and Armenian traditions, restored a measure of Albanian kingship while expanding control across parts of Arran between roughly 893 and 897. Descended from Mihranid princely lines, he operated at the intersection of Georgian, Armenian, and Arab frontier politics.

His brief royal restoration shows how Caucasian dynasts could revive ancient titles amid Abbasid provincial flux. Hereti’s position between Kakheti and Arran made such experiments strategically sensitive.

Hamam is a fleeting but symbolic restorer of Albanian royal dignity.
